test_title: SSC Stenographer 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

Devotional songs are sung superbly by Sastri.

options.text: Sastri has been singing devotional songs superbly.
Sastri has superbly sung devotional songs.
Sastri is singing devotional songs superbly.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "Sastri sings devotional songs superbly."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "devotional songs" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "sings" to "are sung" (present simple passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "Sastri."
 
• Ensure the adverb "superbly" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Sastri sings devotional songs superbly."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"Sastri has been singing devotional songs superbly." – This indicates a continuous action in the present perfect continuous tense, which is not necessary here.
 
• **Option 2: **"Sastri has superbly sung devotional songs." – This is in the present perfect tense, which is not the correct tense for the given sentence.
 
• **Option 3: **"Sastri is singing devotional songs superbly." – This indicates an ongoing action in the present continuous tense, which does not match the original passive sentence.
